documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, visit 02/14/2023.
Type 1 diabetes, about 9 months from diagnosis. A1c from November near goal. Log shows steady fasting values on glargine 22 units at bedtime; meal doses at 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate working well. Occasional mild lows after afternoon walks, self-treated. No severe hypoglycemia.
Feet normal. No change in insulin.
Allergies: NKDA. Meds: insulin glargine 22 units qHS, insulin lispro 1:10 with meals, levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.
Return 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical, first since her diabetes diagnosis last May.

Interval: type 1 diabetes, followed by endocrinology (glargine 22 at night, lispro by carb ratio). Doing well, no severe lows, feels like it's part of the routine now. Thyroid stable on 75 mcg.
Meds: insulin glargine 22 units qHS; insulin lispro 1 unit/10 g with meals; levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. NKDA.
SH: still teaching, coaching math team this spring. Never smoker. Rare wine. Exercise: walks after school.
Gyn: LMP 2 weeks ago, regular. Pap due.
ROS: no vision change, no numbness in feet, no chest symptoms.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Fundi not examined, has outside eye exams. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, monofilament intact, DP pulses 2+ bilaterally. Insulin sites without lipohypertrophy. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap collected.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes: A1c, urine microalbumin, CMP, lipids today. Eye exam due July.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH.
3. Cervical screening: Pap today.
4. Imms: flu/COVID current; PCV20 and hep B series done.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maya. Pap is normal. A1c is under 7, kidney screen for protein is normal, cholesterol, thyroid, blood counts and chemistries all fine. Next Pap in 3 years. I'll copy endocrinology.

documents.title: Re: Physical results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Happy to finally see a 6 in front of that A1c.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 3:30. Called, voicemail. She texted back at 4:50: finals week, lost track of the day, apologized. Rescheduled to September after school starts.

documents.title: Ophthalmology eye examination
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology annual diabetic exam, 07/20/2023.
Acuity 20/20 each eye. Anterior segment normal. Dilated exam: retina without hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization; no macular edema.
Assessment: type 1 diabetes without retinopathy.
Return 1 year. NKDA.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u T1DM and hypothyroidism (rescheduled from June).

S: She wants to start trying for a baby this winter. Asking what she should do first. Sugars steady per her, no lows needing help. Thyroid symptoms none.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1 u/10 g carbs, levothyroxine 75 mcg. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Heart and lungs normal. Feet intact.

A/P
1. Preconception, with type 1 diabetes and hypothyroidism: start a prenatal vitamin with iron daily now. A1c and TSH today. Asked her to see endocrinology before trying, since tight control before conception matters; she will call them this week. Once pregnant, call us and we'll get her to obstetrics early.
2. T1DM: per endocrinology.
3. Hypothyroidism: 75 mcg.
Flu/COVID next month. RTC after she hears from endocrinology or with a positive test.

documents.title: Endocrinology preconception visit
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, 09/26/2023.
Seen for planning before pregnancy. Type 1 diabetes since 05/2022; your recent A1c is at target for conception. Hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg; TSH in range.
Reviewed glucose goals in pregnancy, more frequent checks, earlier and more frequent visits with us once pregnant, and how low blood sugars can become more common in the first trimester.
No insulin changes: glargine 22 units at bedtime, lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate. Already taking a prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Please have her call when she has a positive test.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu shot left deltoid, updated Pfizer COVID right deltoid. Not pregnant per pt, trying. Both safe either way, reviewed. Left after 15 minutes without issue.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! Two positive home pregnancy tests this weekend. Last period started November 16. I already messaged endocrinology. What do I do next?

documents.title: Re: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Come in next week so we can confirm it, check your thyroid, and get you set up with obstetrics. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin. If you have trouble with low sugars before then, call endocrinology the same day.

documents.title: Pregnancy Confirmation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: LMP 11/16/2023, about 4.5 weeks. Positive home tests. Mild nausea in the evenings, no vomiting, no bleeding or cramping. Sugars running a little lower; she has cut her lunch lispro slightly on endocrinology's advice. Taking prenatal vitamin and levothyroxine daily.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10 with meals, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Well. Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P
1. Early intrauterine pregnancy presumed, G1, with pre-existing type 1 diabetes: referral to obstetrics (high-risk practice) placed today. Endocrinology aware.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today. Continue 75 mcg.
3. A1c today for obstetrics and endocrinology.
Reviewed nausea measures and to keep glucose tabs close.

documents.title: Obstetrics new prenatal visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Maternal-fetal medicine / obstetrics, new OB visit 01/09/2024.
G1P0 at 7 weeks 5 days by LMP; dating ultrasound concordant, single live intrauterine pregnancy. EDD 08/22/2024.
History: type 1 diabetes (endocrinology co-managing), autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg. No surgeries. NKDA.
Prenatal labs: blood type, antibody screen, CBC, rubella, syphilis, hepatitis B, HIV and urine culture all unremarkable.
Plan: routine prenatal care with closer diabetes surveillance in partnership with endocrinology. Visits every 4 weeks for now.

documents.title: Ophthalmology eye examination
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology, 02/15/2024. First-trimester dilated exam for a patient with type 1 diabetes, now pregnant. Acuity 20/20 OU. Fundus: no retinopathy, no macular edema either eye.
Plan: repeat in the third trimester only if symptoms; otherwise routine annual exam. NKDA.

documents.title: Endocrinology visit in pregnancy
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, 03/19/2024. Type 1 diabetes in pregnancy, 17-18 weeks. Doing well; glucose log largely in the pregnancy targets. Nausea settled. No severe hypoglycemia.
Insulin: glargine 22 units at bedtime, lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; we expect needs to rise in the second half and will see her every 2-4 weeks.
Also on levothyroxine 75 mcg and a prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 21-22 weeks, G1. Feeling movement. OB visits on schedule. Seeing endocrinology every few weeks; no insulin dose changes on the list so far.
No headaches, no swelling, no vision change. Taking levothyroxine apart from the prenatal.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP as charted, normal. Gravid abdomen. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism in pregnancy: TSH today.
2. T1DM in pregnancy: A1c today, results to OB and endo.
3. Tdap will be done at obstetrics in the third trimester.
See her after delivery.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Obstetrics prenatal visit 05/31/2024, 28 weeks. Tdap given, left deltoid. Fundal height appropriate. Fetal heart tones normal. Continue routine visits and diabetes co-management with endocrinology. NKDA.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request, levothyroxine 75 mcg #90. Last TSH April, in range. Approved per PCP protocol, 90 days with 3 refills.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: hospital obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 08/23/2024, discharged 08/25/2024.

Patient: 28-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks 1 day.
Presentation: contractions about every 5 minutes for six hours; membranes ruptured spontaneously two hours before she arrived. Prenatal course uncomplicated and prenatal labs unremarkable.
History: type 1 diabetes; autoimmune hypothyroidism. No surgeries. Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units subcut at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals at 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol in pregnancy. Teaches mathematics.

Admission findings: BP 120/78, HR 88, temperature 37.2 C (99.0 F). Fetal heart rate tracing reassuring. Sterile speculum exam: clear fluid. Cervix 6 cm, 90% effaced, vertex at -1 station. Recheck four hours later: 7 cm, 100% effaced.
Labor progressed and she had a normal spontaneous vaginal delivery of a healthy liveborn infant. Insulin per the inpatient protocol during labor, with endocrinology input; home doses resumed after delivery.

Postpartum course uncomplicated. Breastfeeding. Discharged home postpartum day 2.

Diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered; normal spontaneous vaginal delivery; type 1 diabetes; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: as above.
Follow-up: obstetrics 6 weeks; endocrinology 2-3 weeks; primary care as scheduled.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2.5 weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery (8/23, discharge summary reviewed). Baby with her in the car seat, sleeping. On maternity leave until November.

S: Breastfeeding going well. Bleeding light. Sleeping in short stretches. Sugars "all over the place for a week" after delivery, now steadier; endocrinology saw her last week and kept her on the usual glargine 22 and lispro by carbs. No lows needing help. Mood good, tired.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin (continuing while nursing). NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Well, tired. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, uterus not palpable. No calf tenderness or edema.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Postpartum, vaginal delivery: recovering well. OB visit at 6 weeks.
2. T1DM: A1c today; endocrinology follows.
3. Hypothyroidism: TSH today, continue 75 mcg.
4. CBC for postpartum blood count.
5. Mood screen low; reviewed postpartum mood warning signs, she knows to text me.
Flu and COVID in October.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid and 2024-25 COVID vaccine R deltoid. Breastfeeding, both fine with nursing, reviewed. Baby along for the visit. No reaction during 15-minute wait.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, 11/15/2024. Three months after vaginal delivery, breastfeeding. Glucose control back to her pre-pregnancy pattern; occasional mild lows after night feeds, managed with a bedtime snack. No severe hypoglycemia.
Plan: glargine 22 units qHS and lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate, unchanged. Levothyroxine 75 mcg. Return 3 months; earlier if planning another pregnancy.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Cancelled visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow, childcare fell through. Will message to rebook after the holidays.

documents.title: Surprise
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So... positive pregnancy test tonight. Wasn't exactly the plan this soon! Last period was November 29. Still nursing. Can I use the appointment I cancelled to come in?

documents.title: Re: Surprise
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. Front desk will call you with a time next week. Keep the prenatal vitamin going, let endocrinology know today, and call them if lows become more frequent.
